body:
WHAT
TaskStop asks the BackgroundManager to stop a background task by id. If the task was running it is stopped and the tool says 'Stopped task <id>.'. If the id exists but is already finished it reports the status; if the id is unknown it says so. Both non-running cases are returned as tool errors with plain text, not thrown.

WHY
Without it a runaway background command or monitor could not be cancelled, and a thrown exception on an already-finished id would make the agent retry needlessly.

WHERE
engine/tools/src/taskControl.ts — taskStopTool (stopSchema, permissionClass 'execute'), execute(): ctx.session.background.stop(id) then background.get(id) for the message. engine/core/src/scheduling/background.ts — BackgroundManager.stop() (returns false unless status is 'running').

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Launch a fake running job; TaskStop returns content 'Stopped task <id>.', the handle's stop() ran and background.get(id).status is 'stopped'.
2. Finish a job via onExit(0) then TaskStop it; assert isError:true and content 'Task <id> was not running (status: completed).' and no exception.
3. TaskStop 'monitor_zzz' (unknown) resolves with isError:true and 'No background task with id monitor_zzz.'.
4. TaskStop the same id twice; the second call reports 'status: stopped' rather than stopping again (stop() ran exactly once).
5. Start a real Bash background 'sleep 20' and TaskStop it; assert the process is no longer alive.
